behavior: package.json postinstall automatically runs the bundled Node script; the public module is an inert proxy facade.
Copies nine npm lifecycle/configuration values and the dynamically named scoped-registry override; CI/orchestrator names are reported as presence flags.
Walks up to eight parent directories, reads consuming package.json, and reports its identity, path, dependency field and declared range.
Reads /.dockerenv presence and /proc/1/cgroup for container classification.
Collects host/user IDs, home/current/install directories, OS/runtime/CPU/memory/uptime and network interface IP/MAC/CIDR data.
Collects resolver addresses and performs reverse DNS to attach internal host names.
Serializes the report and POSTs it to collector.oob.s4yhii.com:443/_npm-poc/beacon with swallowed errors and a five-second timeout.
Performs a secondary DNS lookup with package identity in a label under the collector OOB zone.
limits: Static analysis only; no package installation, script execution, endpoint request or remote payload download.
No evidence of credential-file theft, arbitrary command execution, persistence or bulk environment-value copying.
The secondary DNS query reports package identity; it does not encode host identity.
Source and documentation claim coordinated disclosure; those claims do not establish authorization and cannot suppress behavioral findings.
changes: Removed both source-shape research-beacon exceptions and all consumers.
Converted the package research-authorization exception to a notable claim and removed research-claim exclusions from suspicious OOB surveys.
Retained notable disclosure metadata and ordinary capability evidence; hostile and suspicious severity is determined by collection, transfer and installation behavior.
Moved hostname/OOB/HTTP proximity from hostile exfiltration to suspicious discovery, preserving behavioral matches and updating all six exact consumers.
Converted the VS Code research-canary exception to a notable claim and removed every suppression reference.
